subject: Clarify buyer approval tiers & term options for AWS private offer
messages:
From: Jonathan Smith <jonathan.smith@acmehealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer details & approvals (Acme Health)

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to pull together the ask so we can move toward a private offer in AWS Marketplace. A few quick clarifying questions we need answered before we kick off legal:  

- Recommended term lengths for an entry pilot (6 months) vs production (12/24 months). Any pricing delta for 24-month?
- Are we able to structure activation so individual BU purchases roll up under one PO, or does each BU need separate approval in Marketplace? We have 3 BU approvers (IT, Security, Procurement) and want to understand buyer seniority requirements.
- Required evidence for technical gating: do you need SOC2 report and an on-boarding checklist? We can attach things once we see the activation flow.

We have the internal target to finalize commercial terms by end of next week. Can you confirm who on your side will sign / approve the private offer and whether you can include a two-week activation SLA?

Attached: Acme_RFP_requirements.pdf (high level).

Appreciate a quick sketch so we can escalate internally.

Best,
Jonathan
Jonathan Smith
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Health

----

Attachment: Acme_RFP_requirements.pdf (application/pdf, 1.2MB)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Jonathan Smith <jonathan.smith@acmehealth.com>
Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer details & approvals (Acme Health)

Jonathan — thanks for the clear list. TL;DR below and details after.

TL;DR
- Pilot: 6 months is fine; we typically price pilot at list with a small usage credit — 10-15% off list for 6-mo pilots.
- Production: 12 months (standard) or 24 months (discounted ~18-25% depending on commit).
- Marketplace activation: you can have one umbrella PO if you choose to use consolidated billing/account mapping, but buyer approval windows depend on how your AWS account structure is set up. If each BU has separate AWS payer accounts, each BU approver will need to sign the Private Offer.
- Approvals we see commonly: Procurement + BU finance for purchase; IT for technical scope; Security reviews SOC2 and may request an onboarding proof-of-concept.
- We will provide SOC2 and an onboarding checklist; I can also share a short activation playbook.

What we need from you
- Confirmation of whether you want a single consolidated private offer or separate POs per BU. If consolidated, provide the payer account ID and the list of BU billing aliases.
- Target term and committed monthly/annual spend for discount sizing.

Operational items / who signs
- Commercial signoff: me (jonas) under delegated sales authority up to $500k ARR; for larger commitments I’ll need signoff from Vivek (cc’d) and Sales Ops (Rachel).
- Legal redlines: we’ll route through our Legal team; we normally accept AWS Marketplace standard private-offer terms with a few negotiated clauses for Support SLAs and data handling.

SLA note: Two-week activation SLA is reasonable on our side for technical enablement; Marketplace activation timing can be affected by buyer-side approval cadence. We’ll commit to a technical onboarding window of 10 business days after acceptance, assuming approvals complete.

Attaching a pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx that lays out delta by term and commit band for quick reference.

Next steps
1) Can you send the payer account ID and confirm whether consolidated billing is possible (reply to this thread)?
2) If consolidated, I’ll prepare a preliminary private-offer price sheet for your internal review and a DocuSign link for acceptance.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if that helps — propose Tue or Wed.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 34KB)

From: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 14:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private offer details & approvals (Acme Health)

Jonas — quick internal notes before we finalize the sheet:

- Finance: for anything >$400k ARR we need Finance ops to pre-approve revenue recognition cadence and invoicing terms. Vivek, can you confirm if we can support net-60 for this account?
- Legal: they will push back on indemnity/limitation language if customer requests non-marketplace terms. We should avoid custom legal until they signal specific redlines.
- Marketplace ops: if Acme wants consolidated billing across 3 BU payer accounts we will need the marketplace team to map the buyer identity; that can add 3-5 business days.

Also, given they asked about a 2-week activation SLA, recommend we mark that as contingent on timely BU approvals and completion of security checklist. I can draft the activation playbook and include a checklist item they must complete.

Vivek — tagging you for the $/term discount band. I propose we offer: 6-mo pilot: 10% credit; 12-mo: 15% on committed spend; 24-mo: 22% subject to $X commit. If that sounds OK I’ll incorporate into the DocuSign.

Rachel
Rachel Kim
Head of Sales Ops | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private offer details & approvals (Acme Health) — draft & next steps

Jonathan — following our internal check I’m attaching a draft private-offer summary and next steps. Key points:  

- Pricing: Pilot (6 months) = list with 12% usage credit; Production 12-mo = 15% off list; 24-mo = 22% off list subject to $250k ARR commit. See attached pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx for bands.
- Term: We can do 6 / 12 / 24 — pricing delta included.
- Buyer approvals: If you choose an umbrella private offer mapped to a single payer account ID, only the designated payer account signer needs to accept the private offer. If each BU uses its own payer account, each BU signer will need to accept separately.
- Activation SLA: Redwood commits to a 10-business-day technical onboarding after acceptance, contingent on receipt of SOC2 (we’ve attached our SOC2 summary) and completion of the onboarding checklist. Marketplace activation (mapping the private offer to payer accounts) typically takes 2-5 business days once buyer signs.

Action items for Acme:
1) Confirm whether you want one consolidated private offer or separate offers per BU (reply with payer account ID / BU list).
2) Confirm target term and approximate committed spend so we can lock discount band.
3) If you want net-60 invoices, say so now and we’ll route to Finance Ops for approval (this may require an additional underwriting step).

I’ve created a DocuSign pre-fill for the private offer so we can capture acceptance and start Marketplace activation immediately: https://www.docusign.com/s/embedded/ABC1234

If you prefer a call, we’re available Wednesday 10am PT or Thursday 2pm PT.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this over the finish line.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
